project.name: dotfiles
project.description: Personal chezmoi-managed dotfiles for macOS and Ubuntu client and server machines, with home/ as the public source state and setup.sh as the bootstrap entry point. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

layers.name: Bootstrap and Installation
layers.description: Public chezmoi source selection, platform installers, guarded run-once templates, verified downloads, and private-state restoration boundaries.

layers.name: Managed Configuration
layers.description: Manifest-owned agent settings, generated profiles, shell plugin configuration, tool pins, editor preferences, and repository analysis settings.

layers.name: Agent Runtime and Messaging
layers.description: Deployed Claude/Codex hooks and shared skill links, SQLite-backed agmsg delivery, Herdr agent workspaces, and permission-gate entrypoints.

layers.name: Context Persistence
layers.description: Repository-local CompactionDB ingestion, redaction, durable event storage, recall and recovery, plus installed-runtime notification adapters.

layers.name: Shell and Desktop Runtime
layers.description: Interactive shell startup, aliases and prompts, developer navigation helpers, Git and SSH preferences, and desktop application integration.

layers.name: Maintenance Tooling
layers.description: Agent asset generation and updates, runtime health and review checks, explicit tool upgrades, documentation builds, and scheduled usage reporting.

layers.name: CI and Infrastructure
layers.description: GitHub Actions jobs, Make task entrypoints, the Ubuntu test container, and opt-in Home Manager/nix-darwin package infrastructure.

layers.name: Behavioral Tests
layers.description: Platform Bats fixtures and Python unittest suites covering installation safety, deployed state, agent messaging, runtime repair, and workflow policy.

layers.name: Documentation and Workflow Guidance
layers.description: Operator setup guides, agent skill/rule documentation, hardening plans and acceptance evidence, and the documentation site's presentation assets.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand this chezmoi-managed environment for macOS and Ubuntu client/server machines. It introduces the public home directory source, private-state boundaries, and the update and verification workflows that connect the rest of this tour.

tour.title: Safe Bootstrap Entry
tour.description: Follow setup.sh from the README's installation instructions to see how a new machine acquires its platform dependencies and verified chezmoi executable. The bootstrap previews destination changes and refuses local drift before applying managed files, making preservation of existing machine state part of installation rather than an afterthought.

tour.title: Source and Privacy Boundaries
tour.description: After bootstrap, trace how .chezmoiroot selects home as the public source state and the configuration template collects identity and machine-role choices. The private chezmoi initializer is a separate component, so public configuration and private state are not one undifferentiated deployment tree.
tour.languageLesson: Chezmoi source names and Go templates describe deployed paths and conditional content; a source filename is not always the filename installed in the user's home directory.

tour.title: Pinned Developer Toolchain
tour.description: With the destination model established, examine the mise installer and shared tool configuration. These files separate acquiring the tool manager from declaring developer and agent tool versions, while the installer-pins file records versions and checksums used by other managed installers.

tour.title: Interactive Shell Runtime
tour.description: The installed toolchain becomes visible through shell startup. Compare the minimal environment used by every zsh instance with interactive initialization, then follow the Sheldon template that selects shared, platform-specific, and machine-role plugin sources.
tour.languageLesson: Zsh reads .zshenv for non-interactive shells too, whereas .zshrc is for interactive sessions; keeping their responsibilities separate avoids surprising remote-command behavior.

tour.title: Centralized Agent Configuration
tour.description: The same managed-state approach extends from shells to Claude and Codex. Read the agent architecture guide alongside the central manifest and generator to see how model profiles, hooks, plugins, and MCP definitions become agent-specific outputs instead of independently maintained settings.

tour.title: Agent Workspaces and Messaging
tour.description: Configured agents run in Herdr panes and coordinate through agmsg rather than sharing an implicit conversational state. Follow the pane launcher, the SQLite message sender, and the dispatch wrapper to distinguish storing a message from waking a worker and verifying receipt.

tour.title: Permission Decision Boundary
tour.description: Agent coordination does not itself grant permission to execute an operation. The permgate entrypoint evaluates requests against deterministic policy and optional metadata-only classifiers, while the policy keeps both provider classifiers disabled until their enablement requirements are met.

tour.title: Durable Session Context
tour.description: Next, follow how agent events survive beyond an individual session. ContextDB ingests hook payloads through a durable spool, sanitizes sensitive content, persists events and memories in SQLite, and reconstructs recovery context for later sessions.

tour.title: Maintenance and Drift Repair
tour.description: Return to the Makefile to connect the installed components into everyday operations; it is the graph's broadest task entrypoint. Asset updates, explicit tool upgrades, and runtime drift checks are separate responsibilities, allowing configuration convergence and targeted repair without treating every update as an upgrade.
tour.languageLesson: A Makefile can act as a task interface as well as a build graph: phony lifecycle targets name operations whose success is not represented by a generated file.

tour.title: Optional Nix Package Layer
tour.description: The flake offers an additional, opt-in package-management path alongside the primary bootstrap workflow. Its Home Manager module deliberately leaves dotfile ownership with chezmoi, so introducing Linux or Darwin package profiles does not imply transferring control of the home source tree.

tour.title: Verification and Review Gates
tour.description: Finish by connecting lifecycle behavior to its evidence: focused Python suites exercise runtime convergence and supply-chain requirements, while GitHub Actions route changes into platform tests and conditional Nix evaluation. The Ubuntu container provides a reproducible test environment, and the review guard separately checks whether changed paths require valid review evidence.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions separates event triggers, parallel jobs, and sequential steps; changed-path conditions determine which validation branches actually execute.
